{{Short description|American mathematician (1925–2019)}}
'''George Finlay Simmons''' (March 3, 1925<ref>WWII Draft Registration Card</ref> – August 6, 2019)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n81062366/|title=Simmons, George F. 1925- (George Finlay) [WorldCat Identities]|website=Worldcat}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.coloradocollege.edu/newsevents/newsroom/professor-emeritus-of-mathematics-george-simmons-passes-away|title = Professor Emeritus of Mathematics George Simmons Passes Away - Colorado College| date=7 August 2019 }}</ref> was an American [[mathematician]] who worked in [[topology]] and [[Mathematical analysis|classical analysis]]. He is known as the author of widely used textbooks on university mathematics.

== Life ==

He was born on 3 March 1925 in Austin, Texas.

He received his BS degree from [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1946. He received his MS degree from [[University of Chicago]] in 1948. After finishing his PhD from [[Yale University]] in 1957, he joined [[Colorado College]] as a lecturer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://proofwiki.org/wiki/Mathematician:George_Finlay_Simmons|title=Mathematician:George Finlay Simmons – ProofWiki|work=proofwiki.org}}</ref>

From 1957 to his death in 2019, he taught at a number of universities, which include [[Williams College]], the [[University of Rhode Island]], Yale University, the [[University of Maine]], and the University of Chicago.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.coloradocollege.edu/academics/dept/mathematics/timeline/faculty/Simmons.html|title=Professor George Simmons • Mathematics & Computer Science Colorado College|work=coloradocollege.edu|access-date=2017-02-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160917125621/https://www.coloradocollege.edu/academics/dept/mathematics/timeline/faculty/Simmons.html|archive-date=2016-09-17|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Quotes==
In the [[algebra]] introduction of his book ''Precalculus Mathematics in a Nutshell'', Professor George F. Simmons wrote that the [[New Math]] produced students who had "heard of the [[commutative law]], but did not know the [[multiplication table]]."<ref>{{cite book|title = Precalculus Mathematics in a Nutshell: Geometry, Algebra, Trigonometry: Geometry, Algebra, Trigonometry|publisher = [[Wipf and Stock Publishers]]|year = 2003|chapter = Algebra &ndash; Introduction|chapter-url = https://books.google.com/books?id=dN1KAwAAQBAJ&pg=PA33|page = 33|isbn = 9781592441303|author-link = George F. Simmons|first = George F.|last = Simmons}}</ref>
